newsitem.title: USA: Indenet to cut workforce, take Q3 charge.
newsitem.headline: Indenet to cut workforce, take Q3 charge.

text.p: IndeNet Inc said Tuesday it plans to integrate five previously acquired companies and cut its workforce by 28 percent.

The company said in a statement it will take a third quarter one-time, non-cash charge composed of a write-down of goodwill and other depreciable assets of about $8.5 million as part of the integration plan. The result of this write-down will cut future amortization expense by about $800,000 per year. The company said the initiative should reduce annualized operating expenses by about $8 million.

The company said the integration should also boost revenues. Indenet said it will reserve about $1.6 million in the third fiscal quarter ended December 31, 1996, and will not incur future period expenses related to the plan.
Indenet said it will cut its work-force by 21 percent in February with a further cut of seven percent by April 1997.

The head-count reduction to 445 from 610 will result in savings of about $6.3 million annually. Secondarily, consolidation of research and development as well as marketing will result in additional cost savings, the company said.
The company also said it will reduce its facilities to 11 from 19 by the end of the year which will cut costs by about $600,000 annually.

Further economies in accounting, administration and management, with planned cost reductions of $250,000 annually, are targeted for completion by March 1998, the company said. Automation efficiencies from using digital network deliveries and electronic order processing are planned with a cost reduction target of $500,000 annually by March 1998.
Indenet said the five acquired companies will be merged into two operating divisions.
